title: Fleet resilience: order commitment ledger & runway model
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet models short-to-medium term runway for GPU capacity across regions (us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1, apac1). It ties open order tranches to expected arrival windows, vendor SLA variability, and internal burn-rate scenarios by workload class (Realtime, Batch, Eval). Objective: produce a prioritized commit ledger and a set of fallback lanes that can be triggered when lead-time slippage or surge demand occurs.

Key definitions / conventions used in this sheet:
- SKU: vendor model + memory + form factor (e.g., A100-80GB-PCIe, H100-80GB-SXM).
- Tranche: single PO/commit to a vendor, assigned a tranche id (T-YYYYQX-##).
- Runway days: (Total available GPU hours in region) / (forecasted hourly burn). Burn computed per workload class then summed.
- Lead time window: earliest/most-likely/latest arrival dates (3-point estimate).
- Resilience lane: pre-authorized fallback (spot borrow, cross-region burst, compatible-sku swap).

Executive view (summary rows):
- Current installed fleet (physical GPUs, usable after reserve): 6,420 units (global)
- Committed but not received: 3,750 units (11 tranches)
- Net pipeline by quarter: Q4-2025 +1,200, Q1-2026 +1,150, Q2-2026 +1,400 (subject to LT variance)
- Baseline runway (median lead times, baseline demand): 74 days global
- Stress runway (high demand + latest lead times): 31 days global

Per-region snapshot (text-table excerpt):
Region | Installed | Committed | Median LT days | Baseline-runway-days | Stress-runway-days
us-east1 | 2,600 | 1,250 | 65 | 86 | 38
us-west1 | 1,500 | 900 | 72 | 58 | 24
eu-west1 | 1,200 | 400 | 85 | 64 | 28
apac1 | 1,120 | 200 | 110 | 52 | 19

Tranche ledger (sample rows, full sheet has all):
- T-2025Q4-01 | Vendor: OrionTech | SKU: H100-80GB-SXM | Qty: 600 | Ordered: 2025-09-14 | ETA earliest: 2025-11-20 | ETA likely: 2025-12-18 | ETA latest: 2026-01-22 | Region allocation: us-east1 (60%), us-west1 (40%) | Contingency lane: swap to A100-80GB if H100 delayed > 30d
- T-2025Q4-03 | Vendor: PacificSystems | SKU: A100-80GB-PCIe | Qty: 400 | Ordered: 2025-10-02 | ETA earliest: 2025-12-10 | ETA likely: 2026-01-15 | ETA latest: 2026-03-05 | Region allocation: eu-west1 (100%) | Customs risk flagged (DE); holdback 30 units

Lead-time risk scoring methodology (column explained):
- Score components: vendor SLA variance (30%), historical transit delays (25%), customs/region friction (20%), production rework incidents (15%), final-mile test/BIOS patches (10%).
- Score range 0-100, >70 flagged as high risk. We use a triangular adjustment to move median ETA toward latest when score increases.

Runway sensitivity scenarios captured in the sheet (each scenario is a column set):
1) Baseline: median ETA, forecast demand = trending mean from last 28 days.
2) Demand spike: +25% realtime demand for 21 days (product launch stress).
3) Supply slip: all tranches shift +30% of their median LT (capped at +90 days).
4) Combined worst-case: demand spike + supply slip + 15% SKU mismatch (compatibility rework).

Fallback lanes and activation rules (automated rows in the sheet map triggers to actions):
- If region runway < 21 days AND any inbound tranche has lead-time risk score > 65 -> open cross-region burst (pre-authorized pool) and notify SRE lead.
- If tranche ETA slips past latest ETA in field -> automatically escalate to Vendor Ops and flip 40% of allocations to compatible-sku fallback; log cost delta in 'margin-impact' column.
- If customs watchlist raised for a tranche -> reserve 10% of region installed capacity as buffer; tag tranche as "holds" and prevent assignment to large-batch jobs.

SKU mix guidance (derived from sheet analysis):
- Short-term (next 90d): prioritize higher-margin H100 where low-latency/throughput matters (Realtime). Keep 25% of new arrivals as A100 to satisfy batch/eval workloads and provide swap flexibility.
- Medium-term (Q1-Q2 2026): target a 60/40 H100/A100 active mix in US regions; EU/APAC can skew 50/50 due to customs and procurement friction.

Action items / open decisions captured in doc: 
- [Owner: Marco Alvarez] Confirm customs clearance playbook for PacificSystems tranche by 2026-01-15. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-INFRA-1987.
- [Owner: Emily Chen] Validate cross-region networking bandwidth play for burst lanes (cost estimate + latency impact) by 2026-01-22.
- [Owner: Priya Desai] Circulate vendor SLA variance historical extract and update lead-time risk weights if anomalies found (due 2026-02-02).

Notes for Finance ops (spreadsheet cells explained in prose):
- 'Margin-impact' column computes delta in expected unit economics when fallback SKU used or expedited shipping applied. Formula: (unit_cost_fallback + freight_delta + expedited_fee) - unit_cost_base.
- 'Opportunistic-shelf' column tracks small O(25-100) unit buys from secondary market when lead-time risk >80 for critical tranches. Approval threshold set at $250k per event or head of infra signoff.

Assumptions and caveats:
- This is a working model; vendor ETAs are booking dates not delivery confirmations.
- Beta of auto-fallback policy is enabled in the model but requires manual confirmation for actual POs (policy automation planned for Q2 2026).
- Regional burn uses scheduled jobs + 7-day trailing realtime usage; ad-hoc spikes by partners (internal) might not be fully captured.

Appendix (what the full sheet contains):
- Per-tranche lines (all active and pipeline tranches) with historical vendor on-time % and SLAs.
- Hourly burn curves per region and per workload class (last 90 days + modeled seasonality).
- Cost impact calculator for swaps, expedited shipping, customs brokerage, and depreciation schedule applied to used-gpu buys.
- Audit log table for tranche updates (who changed ETA/qty/status).

Quick context and contact: This doc lives as the canonical procurement runway working sheet for infra. Use it when escalating vendor delays or when approving tranche reassignments. For questions ping #infra-procurement or email priya@redwood.ai.
